doc.title: Ada Rovatti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 13, 2022

title: Berklee scholarship as a baritone beginner
summary: She started sax late, took Berklee and Umbria Jazz courses on baritone and won a scholarship.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Nice. Can you recall what your — I assume you had to do an audition of some sort to get the Berklee scholarship. And do you remember what tunes you played?

Ooh. Well unfortunately I started really late to play saxophone because I was at the end of high school. And I started as a baritone player because I thought maybe the chance to get a scholarship were higher and rightfully so. And I followed a two-week course at Berklee, still has a two-week course at Umbria Jazz, the festival in Italy, and that’s how I followed, I did two courses and at the end I got a scholarship. It was really a beginning but thanks God they found some kind of — I guess talent hidden somewhere because I barely could play and read. I was kind of, really kind of a beginner. I could hear a lot of stuff and I had facility with technique I guess because coming from classical music and playing piano, so I could hear stuff. I had a good ear. But I was really a beginner. But they bet on me and I think I did okay.
